title: Prime Foundation operating budgets are approved one quarter at a time through Atlas edits
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.4.5 sets the rule: after the initial grant, Primes "may request additional grants to their respective Prime Foundations to fund operations and growth," and "In all instances, Sky Governance must consent to the transfer of funds via an Atlas Edit."

The recorded authorizations show what that means in practice. A.2.8.2.2.2.4.4.1 consents to 800,000 USDS per month for three months from Spark's Genesis Capital Allocation; A.2.8.2.2.2.4.5.1.1 raises it to 1,100,000 per month for the next three, now from Spark's Prime Treasury; A.2.8.2.2.2.4.5.1.2, .3 and .4 repeat quarterly through Q3 2026, adding separate lines for the Spark Asset Foundation. A.2.8.2.2.2.4.5.2.1 and .2 do the same for Grove at 800,000 per month, naming the destination multisig.

Two features stand out. Each quarter is a **separate amendment to the Atlas** — the ecosystem's constitutional document carries a rolling record of two Foundations' operating budgets. And the funds are the Prime's *own*: the later grants draw on Spark's and Grove's Prime Treasuries, yet still require Sky Governance's consent to move.

That is the substantive claim. A Prime Foundation cannot fund itself from its own treasury without ecosystem approval, and approval is granted for one quarter at a time. Independence over strategy coexists with quarterly dependence for payroll.

The cost is process volume and an Atlas that accumulates budget line items; the benefit is a hard periodic checkpoint where funding can be adjusted or stopped without invoking any penalty or resolution mechanism. Grants are also delivered through "Spark Spells included in Sky Executive Votes," so each disbursement passes through the same on-chain instrument as everything else.
description: Each grant from a Prime's own treasury to its Foundation is recorded as a separate Atlas provision consented to by Sky Governance, so a Foundation never holds a standing budget.
